sources.entry: multi-scrobbler - Scrobble plays from multiple sources to multiple scrobbling services. (Source Code) MIT Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: multi-scrobbler is a dockerized app that monitors music listening activity from many sources (streaming services, media servers, players) and scrobbles it to many scrobbling clients such as Last.fm, ListenBrainz, and Koito.
summary.what_it_does: It polls or listens to configured Sources, such as Spotify, Jellyfin, Plex, Subsonic-compatible servers, MPD, MPRIS, and VLC, to detect tracks you have played. It then forwards each new play to every Client that Source is configured to feed, including Last.fm, ListenBrainz, Koito, Maloja, Libre.fm, Rocksky, teal.fm, and Discord (Now Playing). Sources can be limited to specific Clients, which allows separate scrobble histories for multiple users. Scrobbles that fail due to network or client problems are queued and retried. Configuration is available through environment variables or JSON, and a web status page shows statistics, logs, and a scrobble audit trail. Sources and Clients can be monitored through webhooks (Gotify, Ntfy, Apprise), healthcheck endpoints, or Prometheus metrics. The README also describes regex or search-pattern rules for modifying data before scrobbling.
use_cases: scrobble plays from Spotify or Plex to Last.fm
keep a self-hosted history of music listening
forward Last.fm or ListenBrainz scrobbles to another service
scrobble for family members or multiple users
scrobble from a Navidrome or Subsonic server
track music played on Sonos, Chromecast, or Kodi
how_to_run: See the Quick Start Guide in the project documentation
Install using Docker images for x86/ARM
Configure Sources and Clients through ENVs or JSON
Open the status page to find the Spotify or Last.fm authorization callback link on first startup
notable: Supports a very wide range of Sources, including Spotify, Jellyfin, Plex, MPRIS, and Sonos
Multiple Clients per Source, with per-Source routing to specific Clients
Queued scrobbles with automatic retry on failure
Mobile-friendly web status page with logs and scrobble audit trail
Credentials persist and can be authorized through the app itself
caveats: Spotify and Last.fm need a one-time authorization through a callback URL on first startup
Setup is configuration-heavy, with separate settings for each Source and Client
The README does not describe platform limits or a paid tier
